paper_title: On the Statistical Query Complexity of Learning Semiautomata: a Random Walk Approach
authors: George Giapitzakis, Kimon Fountoulakis, Eshaan Nichani, Jason D. Lee
statement: • Minimal alphabet size: What is the smallest alphabet size sufficient for SQ hardness? Answering this may require masking constructions (i.e., schemes that assign to each alphabet symbol a binary mask indicating whether that symbol acts as the identity) based on combinatorial designs or deterministic codes, or extending the analysis to transition functions beyond simple transpositions. • Parameter tradeoffs: There may exist a computational tradeoff where reducing the alphabet size necessitates a corresponding increase in input length to maintain hardness.
